constant_found_detail: No fixed 5-6 second value exists on the main-thread prompt path. 27 candidates were swept and dispositioned; the six that were band-capable were each handed to an independent adversarial verifier instructed to REFUTE and to default to ruled-out under uncertainty, and all six returned UNREACHABLE. The crux the brief flagged is resolved: marshal_guard.py:129 (DEFAULT_INLINE_BUDGET_S=5.0) and freeze_chain.py:57 / resilience.py:522 (freeze_threshold=5.0) are pure OBSERVERS - each is compared against an already-elapsed duration, in a finally block or on a daemon watchdog thread, and main_thread.py:326-330 states outright that no bounding is applied because 'any timeout on this path would be a lie'. They MEASURE the band; they cannot CAUSE it. The most freeze-shaped constructs in the tree - ws_bridge.py:528 self.wait(5000), a genuine main-thread QThread.wait of exactly 5.0s, and chat_panel.py:593/:704 subprocess.run(timeout=5) on main - all live in the UNREGISTERED panel surface: packages/synapse.json exposes only $SYNAPSE_ROOT/houdini, whose sole .pypanel loads synapse.panel.synapse_panel, and chat_panel/ws_bridge have zero non-test importers (independently corroborated by the committed harness/notes/panel_capability_matrix.json:665). The N-polls-at-T shape the brief called most likely was swept for specifically and yields only 2.0s, 15.0s and 2.0s - none in band. CONSEQUENCE: the tight band must be explained by a fixed-COST computation whose size is stable turn to turn, not by a hidden timeout - which is exactly why this leg instrumented the result path rather than continuing to hunt literals.

leading_candidate_for_the_tight_band.claim: _find_bridge_instance memoizes only a POSITIVE lookup - the miss path returns None at :71 without setting _BRIDGE_REF - so while no LosslessExecutionBridge exists, the 4000ms QTimer at synapse_panel.py:408-411 walks the ENTIRE Python heap via gc.get_objects(), plus an isinstance per object, on Houdini's main thread, forever, with no stop on hide or close.
leading_candidate_for_the_tight_band.why_it_matters: Heap size is roughly constant within a session, so the walk's DURATION is roughly constant. This is the one mechanism found that produces a tight, repeatable band with no timeout anywhere in it - which is the shape the brief described and the shape the constant hunt just proved cannot come from a literal. It belongs to none of the four known freeze classes and matches the 'Houdini feels sticky while SYNAPSE is open' signature. NOT instrumented by this leg: it is outside the result path the brief scoped. Flagged in FRZ_REPRO.md as a discriminating check to run at the GUI - whether the panel feels sticky WITHOUT sending a prompt separates it from everything on the result path.
